thesis: No NVDA-specific catalyst today — the stock sits near all-time highs with earnings still three weeks out (Aug 26), so today is a macro/semis-sentiment drift session where the AMD hangover and pre-payrolls positioning matter more than any NVDA headline.
day_plan: Treat this as a no-catalyst drift session inside 203-210 with a mild upward lean: NVDA held while AMD broke, ARK added, and the Aug 26 narrative gives dip-buyers cover. Trade the levels rather than a thesis — fade extensions away from VWAP, respect the 13:00 30-year auction and the pre-payrolls afternoon as the two windows where an orderly tape can turn, and keep size small because Friday's jobs report is the real event. Do not chase a gap in either direction before 10:30.
important_news: AMD fell 7-9% after Tue-night earnings despite data-center revenue doubling to $6.7B — the market punished flat 56% gross-margin guidance, i.e. 'growth is getting expensive.' That is the read-through risk for NVDA multiple, but NVDA's margin structure is the counter-argument and NVDA held up Wednesday.

Musk/SpaceX chip-sourcing announcement is cited as the direct trigger for AMD's drop — verify at the open whether it is Nvidia-exclusive (bullish NVDA, explains relative strength) or SpaceX in-house silicon (bearish for the whole merchant-AI-silicon complex, including NVDA over time). This is the single most important unresolved fact this morning.

Sell-side/press previews pushing an Aug 26 blowout (~$95B rev vs ~$91B guide) and a 'low-20s forward P/E' — narrative support for dip-buying, no cash-flow event today, but it sets up buy-the-rumor drift into late August.
Cathie Wood/ARK added to NVDA Wednesday — flow-positive optics, immaterial size for a ~$5T name; treat as sentiment color only.
Insider-selling story ($3.4B across NVDA/PLTR/GOOGL/META) is recycled 10b5-1 filler — ignore unless a fresh Form 4 with unusual size prints today.
CXMT's ~500% IPO debut and $10B DRAM raise — background signal on memory/HBM supply and AI capex intensity; not a same-day NVDA driver.

schedule.event: Premarket tape 07:00-09:30: check NVDA vs AMD, MU, AVGO, SMH/SOXX for whether Tuesday's AMD margin scare is still bleeding into the complex or has been ring-fenced.
schedule.why_it_matters: NVDA's relative strength vs AMD Wednesday is the whole bull case for today. If NVDA is red while AMD stabilizes, the leadership rotation flipped and the drift-up thesis is gone.

schedule.event: Weekly initial jobless claims (plus Q2 nonfarm productivity / unit labor costs).
schedule.why_it_matters: Last macro print before Friday payrolls. A hot claims number pulls rate-cut odds and hits long-duration megacap tech first; NVDA is the highest-beta expression of that.

schedule.event: Cash open / opening range. Gap direction against 206.69 defines the day.
schedule.why_it_matters: With no stock-specific news, the first 15-30 minutes usually sets the day's range for a no-catalyst megacap. Fading the open works far more often than chasing it on days like this.

schedule.event: Opening-range expiry / regime shift — is NVDA above or below the opening 30-min VWAP?
schedule.why_it_matters: On catalyst-free sessions NVDA typically transitions here from headline noise into either a slow VWAP grind (most likely) or a trend day tied to SPX/NDX. Position size should shrink if it's the former.

schedule.event: Treasury 30-year bond auction (quarterly refunding week: 3y Tue, 10y Wed, 30y Thu).
schedule.why_it_matters: A tailing long-bond auction lifts back-end yields and reliably pressures high-multiple AI names in the 13:00-13:30 window. This is the most underappreciated intraday risk today.

schedule.event: Afternoon drift / any scheduled Fed speakers.
schedule.why_it_matters: Thin, headline-sensitive window; the AI complex often makes its high or low of day here on a single tape headline about chip export policy or hyperscaler capex.
Traders flatten AI-beta into Friday's jobs report; late-day supply into the bell is common and can undo a decent 2pm gain.

schedule.event: No NVDA event. Watch any AI-adjacent Q2 reports on tonight's calendar for read-through into Friday's semis open.
schedule.why_it_matters: Overnight semis headlines set NVDA's Friday gap; do not carry oversized swing risk into an NFP morning.

key_levels: 206.69 — prior close and the day's pivot. Holding above it all session is the simplest confirmation the AMD read-through was rejected.
210 — round number and heavy option strike just above; the natural magnet/rejection zone near all-time-high territory. A clean break and hold above on volume is the only genuine breakout setup today.
203-204 — Wednesday's rally base / likely prior-day low zone. First real support; losing it turns the day into a broader AI-complex de-rate, not NVDA noise.
200 — psychological round number and the largest open-interest strike below. A flush there without a macro catalyst is a high-probability mean-reversion bounce spot.
Session VWAP — with no news flow, VWAP is the day's referee: repeated failures beneath it signal institutional distribution near highs, reclaim-and-hold signals passive bid.
SMH / SOXX relative performance — NVDA outperforming a red semis tape is the tell that the SpaceX headline was Nvidia-favorable; underperforming a green tape is the warning.
invalidators: NVDA opens or trades below 203 and fails to reclaim it within the first hour — the AMD margin read-through is being applied to NVDA and the mild-long bias is dead.
Confirmation that Musk's SpaceX announcement is about in-house/non-Nvidia silicon rather than Nvidia exclusivity — that reframes Tuesday's AMD drop as a merchant-silicon TAM story, bearish NVDA.
Initial jobless claims come in materially hot (roughly 260k+) or unit labor costs spike, sending the 10-year yield up 8bp+ — long-duration tech leadership breaks and NVDA underperforms SPX.
AMD trades down another 3%+ today (second-day follow-through rather than stabilization), signaling the market is repricing AI-hardware margins broadly, not just AMD.
NVDA closes red while SMH/SOXX close green — relative-strength thesis invalidated, no reason to hold long exposure into payrolls.
A clean break above 210 with expanding volume — the fade-the-extension part of this plan is wrong; the name is in breakout mode into earnings and shorts should stand aside.
Any fresh chip export-control or China headline — an unscheduled policy shock overrides every level here.
